message.content:
Cells that contain more than one nucleus are called **multinucleated cells** or **polykaryons**.  
In biology the term **syncytium** (plural *syncytia*) is often used to describe a multinucleated cell that results from the fusion of several individual cells.  

Examples of syncytial cells include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Example of multinucleation |
|-----------|-----------------|----------------------------|
| Skeletal muscle fiber | Contractile tissue | A single elongated muscle cell contains dozens–hundreds of nuclei along its length. |
| Osteoclast | Bone resorption | Large bone‑resorbing cells with many nuclei. |
| Syncytiotrophoblast | Placental nutrient exchange | Outer layer of the placenta that fuses into a multinucleated syncytium. |

So if you’re looking for a general term, “syncytium” (or “polykaryon”) is the name for a cell that has multiple nuclei.
